definition: The value a controller is trying to reach. Another word for the target.
The difference between the setpoint and the measured value. Everything in a PID controller is computed from it.
A number you choose that sets how strongly a controller reacts. PID has three: kP, kI and kD.
The part of PID that pushes in proportion to the current error.
The part of PID that reacts to how fast the error is changing, acting as a brake.
The part of PID that reacts to the running total of past error, fixing errors that linger.
When the integral term builds up too much while the output is already at its limit, causing overshoot later.
When a controller asks for more than the hardware can deliver, so the output stays at its limit.
How long a system takes to go from 10% to 90% of the way to its setpoint.
How far a system travels past its setpoint.
How long a system takes to get close to its setpoint and stay there.
The error left over once a system has stopped changing.
Swinging back and forth around the setpoint.
Finding the gain values that make a controller work well on a particular robot.
A sudden spike in the derivative term caused by the setpoint jumping to a new value.
Output calculated from what you already know the system needs, added before any error appears.
